name: ES2004b
method: keypoints = AMI abstractive annotation (decisions, actions, problems, abstract sentences) mapped to keyword groups and spans by Claude (Opus); questions written by Claude from the gold transcript

keypoints.text: The Industrial Designer gave his presentation on the basic functions of the remote.
He presented the basic components that remotes share and suggested that smaller batteries be considered in the product design.
The User Interface Designer presented his ideas for making the remote easy-to-use; he discussed using a simple design and hiding complicated features from the main interface.
The Marketing Expert presented the findings from a lab study on user requirements for a remote control device, and discussed users' demand for a simple interface and advanced technology.
The Project Manager presented the new requirement that the remote not include a teletext function.
The remote will be used only to control television.
The remote must include the company image in its design.
A customer service plan was suggested to make the remote seem more user-friendly, but it was decided that helpful manuals were more within the budget.
It was decided that the group will produce one product design instead of creating alternate designs in an attempt to accomodate different users' preferences.
The marketing will be focused towards a young, business-class buyer.
The remote will feature Video Plus capabilities.
The remote will have a seashell-like shape to accomodate the LCD display and the flip screen.
The remote will be bundled with a docking station to recharge the remote's batteries.
The remote will come with a user-friendly instruction manual.
Multiple casings will be made available.
The Marketing Expert will research consumers' opinions on instruction manuals.
The limitations of the budget will restrict the development of some features; several of the features that the group wanted to include may have to be made simpler to decrease cost.

questions.q: In the remote control design meeting, what technology did the Industrial Designer say most remotes use to send signals to the TV?
In the remote control design meeting, roughly what wireless range did the Industrial Designer give for the infrared signal?
For the remote control project, how many subjects took part in the marketing team's usability lab study?
According to the market research presented in the remote control meeting, what share of users find most remote controls ugly?
In the remote control design meeting, why did the project manager say teletext would not be included?
questions.answer: Consumers consider teletext outdated now that there is the internet.

questions.q: In the remote control meeting, what cheaper alternative to speech recognition did the project manager suggest for finding a lost remote?
questions.answer: A button on top of the TV that makes the remote beep so you can find it.

questions.q: In the remote control market research, which age group mostly wanted an LCD display and speech recognition?
